memo.summary: Context-only committee read: the headline tape is risk-on and the risk radar is calm/receding, but this is not a clean all-clear. The confirmed US regime remains Q2 Reflation at low confidence (0.218) even though its current axes read raw Q3: growth -0.267 and inflation +0.36, with only 1 of 7 confirmation sessions complete. Liquidity is contracting in an orderly, non-stressed drain; credit is healthy and tight; volatility is normalizing; breadth remains broadly intact above the 200-day measure, although the latest session had more decliners than advancers. No market-recovery confirmation chip is fresh, so the recovery context should not be described as confirmed. Factor intelligence is immature: only 10 panel dates, no Pair G records, no factor-attention grading history, no scorecard survivors, and the composite is non-tradeable. This memo annotates existing evidence only and originates no signal, ranking, trade, or probability.
what_fired: World-state display verdict: RISK_ON, score 77, as of 2026-08-27.
Risk radar calm and receding: measured 21-day >=5% pullback rate 13.0% versus 17.8% base rate; this is below-base context, not an edge.
Raw regime axes no longer support confirmed Q2; Q3 transition count is 1 of 7 sessions.
Confluence contradiction: DHI and KDP buy-lane context versus five-day-rising OTM-put skew, as of 2026-08-19.
Briefing-divergence tension: 31 ticker-level demand-versus-supply divergences, including IBM, VSAT, RKLB, and NET.
Factor Pair G did not fire: ledger absent because the panel has fewer than 60 distinct dates.
memo.contradictions_review: Two current graph contradictions were found. First, the briefing contains 31 directional demand-versus-supply divergences; this is a broad tension, not a directional conclusion. Second, DHI and KDP have rising put-skew context against existing buy-lane membership; the legal use is de-escalation only. Separately, the regime label is internally stale relative to its axes: confirmed Q2 versus raw Q3. The factor contradiction ledger is dormant, so absence means insufficient history rather than agreement. Review of the master-brain ledger found many open theses past their check_by dates. Several semiconductor underweight theses deserve explicit review against current mixed evidence: SMH is above its 200-day trend and up 2.27% over 20 days, but down 10.95% over 60 days, semiconductor migration breadth is weak, and the AI-semiconductor thematic falsifier has fired. That is conflicted context, not validation of either side. The open growth-over-value underweight thesis also needs review because IWF/IWD is +2.76% over 20 days while real yields remain restrictive; its dated falsifier must be evaluated rather than informally extended.
